messages:
marta: onboarding polaris-slim-6b int8 experiment. Seeing reduced factuality and early repetition around token 180 in summarization evals. Suspect rotary scaling / fractional-phase rounding during quant.

yuri: Can you share the quant pipeline flags? Did you use per-channel scale or group-wise calibration?

marta: Using quantize.py --mode int8 --calib 2048 --group-size 64 --fp16-to-int8. Conversion cmd:```bash
python quantize.py --model polaris-slim-6b --out polaris-int8 --group-size 64 --no-symmetric
```Quick diff vs fp16 shows attention logits slightly higher on head 10/12 after token 160.

gabe: Higher logits could be from rotary table mismatch or from projection weight rounding. Do you have rotary sin/cos quantized as float16 or re-computed post-quant?

marta: We currently quantize rotary tables along with weights to int8 using the same group-scale. I tried re-computing sin/cos at int16 and embedding them as int16, but sample diffs persisted.

yuri: If rotary scales were quantized with group-size 64 but heads are 32-length, misalignment can cause fractional-phase error. Check if you are applying scale per-64 channels but head boundaries are inside group.

marta: Good point. Head_dim=64, n_heads=12. Group-size 64 should align to head dim, but converter shows group-size applied before the reshape that transposes heads. Might be off-by-one in the packing order.

gabe: Can you run a deterministic forward on a short prompt and dump per-head pre-attention QK dot products for fp16 vs int8? That will show where divergence starts.

marta: Ran that. For prompt "Recent advances in robotics", dotprod_head10[160:190] shows a systematic positive bias of ~0.08 on int8. Rotary_phase_diff_mean ~ 0.012 radians.

infra-bot: eval-job-started id=eval_2026_03_21_42

yuri: Could also be quant rounding bias from asymmetric quantization. Try symmetric per-channel with zero-point 0 for rotary tables and see if bias disappears.

marta: Re-ran with symmetric per-channel for rotary and per-matrix for proj weights. Result: phase_diff_mean -> 3e-4, dotprod bias gone, RougeL back to within 0.05 of fp16 on the small test set.

gabe: So two possibilities: 1) group packing misplaced relative to head stride; 2) asymmetric quant introduced bias. Both explain repetition/hallucination.

yuri: Action items: - marta: push a small fix to quantizer to quantize rotary tables with symmetric per-channel scale by default and add a check that group-size is multiple of head_dim. - gabe: add a smoke test comparing per-head QK means to baseline for first 256 tokens. - infra: add eval job template that runs both symmetric and asymmetric flows for regression detection.

marta: Filed PR draft: https://redwood.internal/prs/ML-9001 - includes unit that asserts rotary_table roundtrip error < 1e-3 after packing.

infra-bot: eval-job-completed id=eval_2026_03_21_42 status=success artifacts=s3://redwood-evals/polaris-slim/2026-03-21/try1.csv

marta: Quick metrics: fp16 rougeL=32.0, int8-default rougeL=30.3, int8-symmetric-rotary rougeL=31.9. So symmetric rotary quant closes the gap. Full eval running.

gabe: Great. After merge, consider adding a permissive transformer-compat header in the packed model that records head_dim, group_size, and a flag whether rotary tables were re-ordered. That will help consumers avoid silent mismatches.

yuri: Agreed. Also document that packer should never reorder channels without updating rotary metadata. We keep tripping over this class of bug.

marta: I'll include metadata and a smokecheck in the PR. Thanks. :thumbsup:
